title: Staff Nurse
description: REKHA HOSPITAL JOB DESCRIPTION STAFF NURSE Department: Nursing Department Designation: Staff Nurse Applicable Areas: General OPD / Casualty / Emergency / General Ward / IPD Reporting To: Nursing In-Charge / Nursing Superintendent Employment Type: Full-Time Location: Rekha Hospital 1. JOB PURPOSE To provide safe, effective and compassionate nursing care to patients attending the hospital through General OPD, Casualty, Emergency, General Ward and Inpatient Department (IPD). The Staff Nurse is responsible for assisting doctors, monitoring patients, administering prescribed medications, performing nursing procedures, maintaining clinical documentation and ensuring quality patient care in accordance with hospital policies and clinical standards. 2. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES A. General Nursing and Patient Care Provide professional, compassionate and patient-centred nursing care. Receive patients and assist with their registration, assessment and clinical requirements. Monitor and record vital signs, including blood pressure, pulse, temperature, respiratory rate and SpO. Assess patient conditions and report any abnormal findings or clinical deterioration to the duty doctor. Assist doctors during patient examinations, consultations and medical procedures. Maintain patient comfort, privacy, dignity and confidentiality. Educate patients and attendants regarding prescribed treatment and nursing care. B. General OPD Responsibilities Assist doctors during outpatient consultations and examinations. Prepare consultation rooms, medical instruments and nursing equipment. Check and record patient vital signs before consultation. Administer prescribed injections, medications and treatments. Perform wound dressing and other authorized nursing procedures. Coordinate with laboratory, pharmacy and diagnostic departments. Maintain OPD nursing records and ensure proper patient flow. C. Casualty and Emergency Responsibilities Receive emergency patients and assist with initial assessment and triage according to hospital protocols. Immediately inform the duty doctor regarding emergency and critical cases. Assist doctors during emergency management and resuscitation. Assist in CPR and Basic Life Support procedures according to current training and competency. Administer prescribed emergency medications and IV fluids. Assist with oxygen therapy, nebulization and other emergency interventions within authorized competency. Monitor emergency patients and immediately report changes in clinical condition. Maintain readiness of emergency equipment, crash carts and emergency medicines. Assist with patient stabilization, admission, referral and transfer procedures. Maintain emergency case sheets and treatment documentation. D. General Ward and IPD Responsibilities Receive admitted patients from OPD, Casualty and other hospital departments. Verify patient identification and complete initial nursing assessments. Monitor patient health conditions and record vital signs at prescribed intervals. Administer oral, injectable and IV medications according to authorized prescriptions and hospital protocols. Monitor IV fluids, infusion pumps and other prescribed treatments. Perform wound dressing, catheter care and other nursing procedures within professional competency. Monitor intake and output, blood glucose and other clinical parameters as prescribed. Assist patients with personal hygiene, feeding, mobility and daily care requirements. Assist doctors during ward rounds and prescribed medical procedures. Coordinate investigations, laboratory reports, radiology and other diagnostic services. Monitor patients for complications and report any deterioration immediately. Maintain medication charts, nursing notes, observation charts and treatment records. Assist in patient transfers between wards, ICU and other departments. Prepare patients for discharge and complete the required nursing documentation. Provide discharge-related nursing instructions as directed by the treating doctor. E. Medication and Clinical Safety Follow medication administration rights and hospital medication policies. Verify patient identity, medication, dosage, route and timing before administration. Check medication expiry dates, storage conditions and availability. Report medication errors, adverse drug reactions and other incidents immediately. Maintain proper records of administered medications and treatments. Follow safe injection practices and infection prevention protocols. F. Infection Control and Hospital Safety Follow hand hygiene and standard infection prevention precautions. Use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE). Follow biomedical waste segregation and disposal guidelines. Maintain cleanliness and hygiene in the assigned nursing area. Follow isolation precautions wherever required. Prevent patient falls, pressure injuries and other avoidable patient safety incidents. Report equipment malfunction, hazards and safety-related incidents to the concerned authority. G. Documentation and Administration Maintain accurate and complete nursing documentation. Update patient case sheets, nursing records and treatment charts. Maintain records of medicines, consumables and nursing supplies. Ensure proper shift handover and communicate pending treatments and important patient information. Maintain patient confidentiality and protect medical records. Coordinate effectively with doctors, nursing colleagues and other hospital departments. Participate in hospital audits, quality activities, training and clinical meetings. Follow hospital rules, regulations, policies and instructions issued by Management and the Nursing Superintendent. 3. EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION GNM (General Nursing and Midwifery) or B.Sc. Nursing. Valid registration with the applicable State Nursing Council. Additional clinical training or certifications as required for the assigned department. 4. EXPERIENCE Freshers and experienced candidates may be considered based on hospital requirements. Relevant clinical experience in OPD, Emergency, General Ward or IPD is preferred. Emergency assignments require appropriate emergency-care training and competency. 5. REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS Knowledge of basic nursing procedures and patient care. Knowledge of vital signs monitoring and medication administration. Knowledge of infection control and biomedical waste management. Ability to recognize and escalate changes in patient condition. Good communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to work in shifts and handle clinical responsibilities. Basic computer and hospital information system knowledge.
